components.purpose: Ask one question — bring this archived agent back? — with what returns, what it costs (a slot), and the binding's honest state said first.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6 — the confirmation-page skeleton. h1 'Reactivate <name>?', the optional problem banner, then the shared ReactivatePrompt. Deliberately a route of its own rather than archive?to=ACTIVE (DL-104: two consequences behind one URL is how someone confirms wording written for the other operation), and deliberately without a confirmation token — reactivating restores a state the user chose before and commits nothing. Unchanged by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person`: this page still spells its problem banner out inline and only on the prompt branch, so the roster-unreadable and no-such-agent branches drop a carried ?problem= (a behavior gap, not styling — the sibling ceremony pages closed the same gap by mounting the shared CarriedProblem on every branch).
constraints: The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

No confirmation token exists on this page by decision (DL-104's sibling reasoning in the route comment) — a design must not add ceremony that implies one, and must not merge this page back into the archive route.

Reactivation returns the agent in its previous configuration — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:211-213 ('it returns to the roster in its previous configuration'); the copy stating that is spec-bearing.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted reactivate back to the person who clicked it.
components.current_implementation: Spelled out inline in the route, not the shared component: a role=alert paragraph, rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary, with the semibold 'Refused: ' prefix. Byte-for-byte what CarriedProblem (carried-problem.tsx) now renders on deploy, undeploy and rebind — this page was outside `the-outcome-reaches-the-person`'s scope, so it holds a hand copy of the shared treatment and mounts it on the prompt branch only.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The refusal must keep returning to this surface with the operation's own reason — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:481-484 ('the user is told, on the surface they acted from … the reason given is the one the operation returned'); the route comment names the alternative as indistinguishable from success.

This banner and CarriedProblem must not be allowed to diverge — a restyle of the bounced-write banner has to reach both, and the honest fix is for this page to adopt the shared component (that is a code change, not a design ticket).
The reason is platform-authored and unbounded — the block must wrap rather than clip, and must not truncate or paraphrase.

components.purpose: What reactivating returns — the configuration it had when archived, at the cost of a slot — then one committing button and one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with agentId and expectedRevision; success lands on /agents/[id], a not-permitted refusal redirects back here with ?problem=

components.current_implementation: Shared ReactivatePrompt (agent-edit.tsx): two plain sentences — what returns and that it takes a slot, split deliberately from the binding claim below them — then BindingSummary, the optional at-capacity notice, and the form's buttons in flex flex-wrap gap-3 (no mobile full-width stack). not-archived replaces everything with a role=alert '<name> is not archived.' and an underlined link back. The submit stays offered even at capacity — capacity warns before the act rather than disabling it, and the refusal path handles the rest.
constraints: The what-returns sentence and the binding sentence are deliberately separate paragraphs — the first is true whatever the binding says, the second is a claim about the binding, and this page is where conflating them cost most (Volatilis, ARCHIVED and ORPHANED). A relayout must not merge them.
Nothing here is styled to look disabled — 'Nothing is styled to look disabled when retrying cannot help' (system.json principle); at capacity the button still works and the platform answers.
Two hidden inputs (agentId, expectedRevision) carry the revision the intent was formed against — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:252-254; the form must keep exactly one submit path.

components.purpose: What the agent is bound to, in words that stay honest when the binding is broken — on the page where reading 'bound to' about an unreadable strategy would cost most.
components.current_implementation: Shared BindingSummary (binding.tsx) in a plain text-sm paragraph. ORPHANED states only what the payload supports: the strategy can no longer be read, and the revision the configuration was materialized from. An unrecognised state renders as the platform's own word, uninterpreted.
constraints: One component for every surface that describes a binding — a design must restyle the shared component, not fork a per-page copy.
The ORPHANED sentence must not gain copy that guesses what the state means — its operational meaning is unestablished.

components.purpose: Say before the act, not after the refusal, that reactivating takes a slot the account does not currently have.
components.current_implementation: role=alert paragraph, rounded-gc-2 border border-border-default p-3 text-sm — a neutral border, not danger and not the notice tokens; the explanation text is the platform-derived capacity sentence.
constraints: Capacity is explained before the work — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:134-136 ('SHALL tell the user before they begin'); this block must stay above the buttons.
Advisory is not failure — 'notice never borrows danger's colour' (system.json principle); this must stay visually distinct from the problem banner above it, which can be on screen at the same time.
role=alert must survive.

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px, DT-0003's token), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. No pending/loading state between click and redirect.
constraints: Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product — not a per-page className.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: Leave the agent archived and go back to it.
components.current_implementation: An anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, DT-0004's hover (border-strong + bg-sunken over duration-fast). Only the prompt branch wears it; not-archived, roster-unreadable and no-such-agent still use plain underlined prose links.
constraints: Must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and a visible peer of the submit (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Tell an operator whose archived agent did not load that it is not gone — the one page where 'gone' is a live worry.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded (why-not-loaded.tsx), a plain mt-2 paragraph under the 'Could not load this agent' heading. Two sentences chosen by cause: BattleGrid refused the authority, or could not be reached.
constraints: The refused/unreachable distinction is spec — openspec/specs/agent-authoring/spec.md:43-52; the reassurance that the agent is not gone matters most here, per the route's own comment, and must survive any rewording.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Reactivate an agent
steps: arrive from the agent page or roster
read what returns, that it takes a slot, and the binding's honest state
land on /agents/[id] with the agent active

flows.name: The reactivate is refused after submit
steps: problem banner states the reason above the still-usable form

flows.name: The bounce lands on a branch that cannot show it
steps: submit; the platform refuses and redirects back with ?problem=
the roster will not load, or the agent is no longer in it
those branches do not render the problem, so the reason for the click is lost — the gap the sibling ceremony pages closed with CarriedProblem

flows.name: The account is at capacity
steps: the capacity notice says so before the act
the button remains offered; a submit that the platform refuses comes back as a problem

accessibility.notes: Problem banner, capacity notice and the not-archived refusal carry role=alert; the problem banner and the capacity notice can be on screen together. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation.
